nodes.label: Loss-Threshold Membership Inference Attack
nodes.rationale: Training examples tend to have lower loss than fresh samples, so a loss threshold can reveal membership when a generalization gap exists.

nodes.label: Generalization Error and Membership Advantage
nodes.rationale: The paper formally connects membership advantage to overfitting and, in some settings, makes the relationship directly proportional.

nodes.label: Feature Influence
nodes.rationale: Influence determines when overfitting produces attribute-inference risk and must be balanced with generalization error.

nodes.label: Malicious Stable-Algorithm Substitution Attack
nodes.rationale: Overfitting is sufficient but not necessary: a nearly stable learner can be maliciously modified to reveal exact membership with little utility loss.

nodes.label: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
nodes.author: Weijia Shi; Anirudh Ajith; Mengzhou Xia; Yangsibo Huang; Daogao Liu; Terra Blevins; Danqi Chen; Luke Zettlemoyer
nodes.norm_label: detecting pretraining data from large language models

nodes.label: Min-K% Prob
nodes.rationale: Unseen text is more likely to contain a few anomalously low-probability tokens, so averaging the lowest-probability token scores emphasizes membership evidence.

nodes.label: Min-K%++: Improved Baseline for Detecting Pre-Training Data from Large Language Models
nodes.author: Jingyang Zhang; Jingwei Sun; Eric Yeats; Yang Ouyang; Martin Kuo; Jianyi Zhang; Hao Frank Yang; Hai Li
nodes.norm_label: min-k%++: improved baseline for detecting pre-training data from large language models

nodes.label: Training Samples as Local Likelihood Maxima
nodes.rationale: Maximum-likelihood training makes training points tend to lie at or near local maxima along input dimensions, turning membership detection into mode identification.
nodes.norm_label: training samples as local likelihood maxima

nodes.label: Membership Inference Attacks against Language Models via Neighbourhood Comparison

nodes.norm_label: membership inference attacks against language models via neighbourhood comparison

nodes.label: Sample-Difficulty Calibration
nodes.rationale: Comparing a target only to an absolute threshold confounds membership with the text's intrinsic complexity.

nodes.label: Reference-Distribution Fragility
nodes.rationale: Reference-model attacks degrade when the data used to train the reference model does not closely match the target training distribution.

nodes.label: ReCaLL: Membership Inference via Relative Conditional Log-Likelihoods
nodes.author: Roy Xie; Junlin Wang; Ruomin Huang; Minxing Zhang; Rong Ge; Jian Pei; Neil Zhenqiang Gong; Bhuwan Dhingra
nodes.norm_label: recall: membership inference via relative conditional log-likelihoods

nodes.label: In-Context Learning as Implicit Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: A non-member context perturbs the predictive distribution of already-memorized member text more strongly than unfamiliar non-member text.

nodes.label: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
nodes.author: Nicholas Carlini; Florian Tramer; Eric Wallace; Matthew Jagielski; Ariel Herbert-Voss; Katherine Lee; Adam Roberts; Tom Brown; Dawn Song; Ulfar Erlingsson; Alina Oprea; Colin Raffel
nodes.norm_label: extracting training data from large language models

nodes.label: Reference-Model Likelihood Ratio
nodes.rationale: Samples that are abnormally more likely under the target than under a separate language model are prioritized as likely memorized training examples.

nodes.label: Perplexity-to-zlib Entropy Score
nodes.rationale: Compression provides a model-independent normalization for intrinsically repetitive text that can otherwise look memorized under raw perplexity.

nodes.label: Differentially Private Training
nodes.rationale: Record-level differential privacy offers formal protection but can increase training cost and reduce utility.

nodes.label: Document Deduplication Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Deduplicating documents empirically reduces memorization risk but cannot prevent all extraction attacks.

nodes.label: Sampling-based Pseudo-Likelihood for Membership Inference Attacks
nodes.author: Masahiro Kaneko; Youmi Ma; Yuki Wata; Naoaki Okazaki
nodes.norm_label: sampling-based pseudo-likelihood for membership inference attacks

nodes.label: Sampling-Frequency Likelihood Approximation
nodes.rationale: By the law of large numbers, empirical generation frequency approximates the model's sequence probability, making overlap a pseudo-likelihood signal without logits.

nodes.label: Membership Inference Attacks against Fine-tuned Large Language Models via Self-prompt Calibration
nodes.author: Wenjie Fu; Huandong Wang; Chen Gao; Guanghua Liu; Yong Li; Tao Jiang
nodes.norm_label: membership inference attacks against fine-tuned large language models via self-prompt calibration

nodes.label: Self-Prompt Reference Model
nodes.rationale: Text sampled from the target model supplies a practical reference dataset whose distribution resembles the private fine-tuning distribution.

nodes.label: Memorization Without Overfitting
nodes.rationale: Practical, regularized LLMs may memorize records before they overfit, so raw probability is an unreliable membership signal.

nodes.label: Window-based Membership Inference Attacks Against Fine-tuned Large Language Models
nodes.author: Yuetian Chen; Yuntao Du; Kaiyuan Zhang; Ashish Kundu; Charles Fleming; Bruno Ribeiro; Ninghui Li
nodes.norm_label: window-based membership inference attacks against fine-tuned large language models

nodes.label: Sparse Extremal Membership Signal
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuning memorization appears in sparse localized token events rather than a uniform shift, so global averaging dilutes the signal.

nodes.label: Min-K%++ Fine-Tuning Adaptation
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: Multiple fine-tuning epochs should strengthen the local-mode signal relative to the single-pass pretraining setting.

nodes.label: Min-K%++ Candidate Ranking for Extraction
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction

nodes.label: Memorized-Span Localization
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: Per-window loss differences identify where a sequence carries fine-tuning membership evidence and provide spans for prefix-prompted extraction.

nodes.label: WBC Source-Identification Caveat
nodes.rationale: The acronym was matched to Window-Based Comparison using the repository configuration key and the paper, but a different private-harness meaning remains possible.

nodes.label: ReCaLL Fine-Tuning Adaptation
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: A fixed outside-the-fine-tuning-set prefix can perturb memorized fine-tuning records and should benefit from stronger multi-epoch memorization.

nodes.label: Membership Confirmation for Extraction Auditing
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction

nodes.label: Verbatim Suffix Regeneration Signal
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: The attack's scoring samples are themselves candidate reconstructions, making high overlap direct evidence of verbatim memorization.

nodes.label: Membership-Score-Only Ethical Safeguard
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: The released tool withholds generated text and exposes only a membership score to reduce extraction misuse.

nodes.label: DP-SGD Membership-Leakage Trade-Off
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: Stronger differential privacy lowers attack AUC but the reported moderate budgets do not eliminate leakage.

nodes.label: Causal-LM Scope Limitation
nodes.source_location: Adaptation for LLM fine-tuning + data extraction
nodes.rationale: The method is designed for causal language models; MLM and sequence-to-sequence extensions are left for future work.

nodes.label: Membership Inference Attacks Background Research Summaries
nodes.norm_label: membership inference attacks background research summaries

nodes.label: Private Aggregated Benchmark Caveat
nodes.rationale: The ten-key evaluation harness was not located publicly and is likely an aggregated private benchmark.

nodes.label: Active Membership Inference Attack Results Report
nodes.norm_label: active membership inference attack results report

nodes.label: Active Membership Inference Attack under Local Differential Privacy in Federated Learning
nodes.author: Nguyen et al.
nodes.norm_label: active membership inference attack under local differential privacy in federated learning

nodes.label: Chosen-Neuron Gradient Membership Test
nodes.rationale: A non-zero gradient indicates that the target-only ReLU neuron activated during the client's local update.

nodes.label: Zero-Threshold False-Positive Artifact
nodes.rationale: Member scores start at 3.297 while non-member scores top out at 3.217, yet treating any nonzero gradient as membership creates seven avoidable false positives.

nodes.label: No-LDP Evaluation Limitation
nodes.rationale: The experiment validates only the attack without local differential privacy and does not exercise the source paper's certified LDP setting.

nodes.label: LOSS Membership Inference on a Federated LLM Results Report
nodes.norm_label: loss membership inference on a federated llm results report

nodes.label: Distribution-Mismatched Loss Threshold
nodes.rationale: The calibration non-members have roughly 0.01 lower intrinsic loss than the target canaries, overwhelming the roughly 1e-4 membership gap and preventing any positive predictions.

nodes.label: Federated Update Dilution
nodes.rationale: Averaging one target client's weak update across four participants and only two rounds suppresses the generalization gap.

nodes.label: Membership-Advantage Definition Caveat
nodes.rationale: The experiment reports balanced accuracy as Adv, whereas Yeom et al. define advantage as TPR minus FPR.

nodes.label: zlib-Entropy Ratio Membership Inference on a Federated LLM Results Report
nodes.norm_label: zlib-entropy ratio membership inference on a federated llm results report

nodes.label: Perfect-AUC Artifact
nodes.rationale: Perfect ordering over only two members and two non-members under a non-training toy scorer most plausibly reflects incidental record compressibility, not memorization.

nodes.label: Out-of-Range zlib Threshold
nodes.rationale: All scores cluster near -0.01593 while the threshold is -0.0058, so the classifier never predicts a member.

nodes.label: Vacuous False-Positive Control
nodes.rationale: Zero false positives arise from predicting non-member for every record, not from successfully normalizing repetitive text.
